ShouldDisappearFromDoom.maps_to: no sim counterpart; the sim has no DoomPower at all
ShouldDisappearFromDoom.rationale: Presentation, and this is the CROSS-BATCH ADJUDICATED verdict on the mechanism (binding rule 3) after two batches disagreed -- recorded as ruled, and independently re-derived before recording. `ShouldDisappearFromDoom` has exactly one reader in the whole game tree: DoomPower.cs:90, and line 90 sits inside the PRIVATE helper `PlayVfx`, which early-returns when the creature has no visual node (DoomPower.cs:82-86). The `flag` it computes is consumed in exactly two places -- `StartDoomAnim(nCreature, flag)` (DoomPower.cs:92) and a Cmd.Wait(0.25f)/Cmd.Wait(1.5f) timing branch (DoomPower.cs:101-111). StartDoomAnim's shouldDie arm (DoomPower.cs:117-134) is `Monster?.OnDieToDoom()`, an AnimDisableUi tween, QueueFreeSafely, a Spine "Hit" trigger, `NCombatRoom.RemoveCreatureNode` (removal of the VIEW node) and an NDoomVfx variant; `OnDieToDoom` is documented at MonsterModel.cs:485-491 as 'Primarily used set up the creature visuals for the Doom vfx', has an empty base body, and its one override (TorchHeadAmalgam.cs:67-79) hides three light nodes. DECISIVE: the kill does NOT consult it -- DoomPower.DoomKill (DoomPower.cs:40-53) is `await PlayVfx(creature); await CreatureCmd.Kill(creature);`, so the Kill is UNCONDITIONAL and outside PlayVfx. The flag therefore gates whether the sprite vanishes with the doom animation, never whether the creature dies or leaves Enemies. Waiver on presentation, matching monster_state_machine N2 and the KinPriest N6 precedent (read the override to the end before verdicting). That the sim has no Doom at all is a secondary observation and is NOT the load-bearing part of this argument.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Hand-rolled port of CeremonialBeast.cs:143-168. Reachable graph: phase 1 STAMP_MOVE (initial) -> PLOW_MOVE -> PLOW_MOVE (self-loop); phase 2, entered only by the stun, BEAST_CRY_MOVE -> STOMP_MOVE -> CRUSH_MOVE -> BEAST_CRY_MOVE. The port's _TRANSITIONS dict is exactly those five edges. Executed, not asserted (verdict rule 5): `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py chain` rebuilds the C# GenerateMoveStateMachine graph node for node on the sim's OWN MonsterMoveStateMachine primitives (so the walk, the repeat rules and the single-NextFloat(total) draw are the audited machinery) and diffs it against the shipped port over 20 turns from an identically seeded RunRngSet. Result: 20/20 turns identical from STAMP, 0 MonsterAi draws on both sides (no branch state exists). The phase-2 entry is verified separately in the guards.

guards.what: How phase 2 is entered: PlowPower.cs:42-46 calls SetStunned() and then `CreatureCmd.Stun(Owner, ceremonialBeast.StunnedMove, BeastCryState.StateId)`; the sim's PlowPower calls `CreatureCmd.stun(self._hooks, self, next_move_key='BEAST_CRY')` (ceremonial_beast.py:41-45)
guards.rationale: Both defer exactly one turn and resume at BEAST_CRY. C# builds a synthetic MoveState('STUNNED', StunnedMove, StunIntent) with FollowUpStateId = 'BEAST_CRY_MOVE' and MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning (monster_state_machine step 40); StunnedMove itself is `IsStunnedByPlowRemoval = false` plus a TriggerAnim (CeremonialBeast.cs:216-220), i.e. no mechanics, so the sim's turn-skip (combat.py:313-329) is the same observable. This unit is the ONE ported caller that passes next_move_key, and it works only because CeremonialBeast is a hand-rolled Monster with a `_move_key` attribute -- that is monster_state_machine G5's dormancy argument and is NOT re-verdicted here. The log-duplication half (G4) cannot be observable on this monster either: it has no RandomBranchState, so no weight reads the state log. Rule 7: PlowPower.cs and sts2_rl/combat.py are hashed in extra_sources.

PROMPT.md bug class 24 -- verdict the code, not the comment. The comment claims PlowPower can interrupt mid-turn; the guard is what matters and it is right: PlowPower's AfterDamageReceived can fire during the beast's OWN attack (a Thorns/retaliate reflect, or any unblocked damage that drops it to <= the Plow amount), and without the guard the _TRANSITIONS advance would overwrite the BEAST_CRY the stun just installed. C# is immune to the same race for a different reason -- SetMoveImmediate replaces the state outright -- so the guard is the port's equivalent, not an extra.

guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:224-243), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit's MaxInitialHp is `=> MinInitialHp`, so the range is the single value 252 and no endpoint can be lost; the check is recorded anyway because an off-by-one would turn a one-element candidate list into an empty one and change which ARM of SetUniqueMonsterHpValue runs (NextItem vs NextInt), which is a stream-position difference even when the HP is identical. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [252,252], observed [252,252], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 252 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:78) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
